steps.title: Saying how you feel
steps.body:
Two ways to say how you are, and French uses them differently from English.

**Être** + adjective, for a state: *je suis fatigué*, *je suis stressé*, *je suis triste*.

**Se sentir**, to feel, for how you feel right now: *je me sens bien*, *je me sens mal*, *je me sens fatigué*.

The adjective has to **agree** with whoever is speaking. A boy writes *je suis fatigué*; a girl writes *je suis fatiguée*. It sounds the same and it is a written mark, so it is free to get right and free to lose.

One to watch: English says *I am cold* but French says **j'ai froid** — literally *I have cold*. The same goes for *j'ai peur* (I am afraid) and *j'ai besoin de* (I need).

visuals.fallback: la santé mentale — mental health; le sommeil — sleep; inquiet — worried; fatigué — tired; détendu — relaxed; triste — sad; le soutien — support.

check.prompt: How would a girl write *I am tired*?
check.solution: The adjective agrees with the speaker, so a girl adds **-e**: *fatiguée*. It sounds identical, but the written mark is there.
options: Je suis fatiguée
Je suis fatigué
J'ai fatiguée
Je me fatigue

steps.title: Reflexive verbs: the extra little word
steps.body:
A **reflexive verb** carries a pronoun that points back at the subject. In English we usually leave it out: *je me couche* is *I go to bed*, not *I put myself to bed*.

You already met these in Year 9 with daily routine, and they run through the whole of this unit.

The pronoun changes with the subject, and it goes **before** the verb:

| | |
|---|---|
| je **me** | nous **nous** |
| tu **te** | vous **vous** |
| il/elle/on **se** | ils/elles **se** |

Before a vowel or a silent *h*, **me**, **te** and **se** shorten: *je m'habille*, *il s'appelle*.

The verb itself then conjugates as normal for its group.

visuals.alt: A table of se coucher in the present tense, with the stem couch- fixed and the endings -e, -es, -e, -ons, -ez, -ent changing

check.solution: With **elle** the pronoun is **se**, and the *-er* ending for elle is **-e**: *elle se couche*.

markScheme.description: Elle se couche à neuf heures

options: Elle se couche à neuf heures
Elle me couche à neuf heures
Elle couche à neuf heures
Elle se couches à neuf heures

steps.title: Se sentir: an -ir verb that behaves
steps.body:
**Se sentir** (to feel) is the verb this topic leans on hardest. It is an *-ir* verb, but not the *-issons* kind: it follows the shorter pattern, like *partir* and *dormir*.

The stem drops the **-tir** in the singular and keeps it in the plural, so listen for that:

*je me sens, tu te sens, il se sent* — then *nous nous sentons, vous vous sentez, ils se sentent*.

With it you can say a great deal:

- *Je me sens bien / mal.*
- *Je me sens fatigué / stressé / détendu.*
- *Je ne me sens pas bien.* — the **ne … pas** wraps around **both** the pronoun and the verb.

That last one is worth learning as a whole phrase. Putting the *ne* in the wrong place is the commonest slip in this topic.

visuals.alt: A table of se sentir in the present tense, with the singular stem sen- and the plural stem sent-

steps.text: Start from the positive: *je me sens bien*
The **ne** goes before the pronoun, not before the verb: *je **ne** me sens…*
steps.note: This is the step people get wrong

steps.text: The **pas** goes after the verb: *je ne me sens **pas** bien*
*Je ne me sens pas bien.* — I don't feel well

check.prompt: Write in French: *I don't feel well.*
check.solution: **Je ne me sens pas bien.** The **ne** comes before **me**, and the **pas** after the verb.

markScheme.description: je ne me sens pas bien

accepted: je ne me sens pas bien

steps.title: Saying what helps
steps.body:
Once you can say how you feel, the next half of the topic is what you do about it.

**Pour** + infinitive means *in order to*: *pour me détendre* — *to relax*. Notice that the reflexive pronoun stays and matches you: **pour me détendre**, not *pour se détendre*, when you are talking about yourself.

**Il faut** + infinitive means *you must* or *it is necessary to*. It never changes: *il faut dormir*, *il faut manger sainement*. The negative is **il ne faut pas** — *you must not*.

**J'ai besoin de** + infinitive is *I need to*: *j'ai besoin de dormir*. Do not drop the **de**.

And **quand** + present lets you set a condition: *quand je suis stressé, je fais du sport*.

visuals.fallback: se détendre — to relax; se coucher — to go to bed; se reposer — to rest; dormir — to sleep; faire du sport — to do sport; écouter de la musique — to listen to music; parler à quelqu'un — to talk to someone; éviter — to avoid.

check.prompt: Complete: *J'ai besoin __ dormir.* Give the missing word.
check.solution: **de** — *j'ai besoin de dormir*. **Avoir besoin** always takes **de** before the infinitive.

steps.title: Building a sentence that scores
steps.body: A one-clause sentence gets you a low mark however correct it is. The way up is to add a reason, then a time phrase, then an opinion. Each addition is a separate mark in the writing paper.

visuals.problem: From three words to a sentence that scores

steps.text: *Je fais du sport.* — correct, but it is one clause and one tense
*Je fais du sport parce que ça me détend.* — a reason with **parce que**
steps.note: Reasons are the cheapest marks in the paper

steps.text: *Normalement, je fais du sport parce que ça me détend.* — a time phrase
steps.note: Normalement, souvent, tous les jours, une fois par semaine

steps.text: *À mon avis, il faut faire du sport, parce que ça me détend et ça réduit le stress.* — an opinion, **il faut**, and two reasons joined with **et**
steps.note: Same vocabulary; four times the credit

check.prompt: Which sentence would score highest in a writing task?
check.solution: It has a reflexive verb, a time adverb and a reason with **parce que**. The others are single clauses, and *c'est bien* adds nothing.

markScheme.description: Je me couche tôt parce que j'ai besoin de dormir

options: Je me couche tôt parce que j'ai besoin de dormir
Je me couche tôt
Je dors
Le sommeil est bien

steps.title: Opinions worth more than c'est bien
steps.body:
Every speaking and writing task wants opinions, and *c'est bien* is the phrase to stop using. Build them in three parts.

**An opinion phrase.** *À mon avis*, *je trouve que*, *selon moi*, *d'après moi*, *je pense que*. Rotate them; repeating *je pense que* four times is marked as a narrow range.

**A precise adjective.** Not *bien* but *essentiel*, *utile*, *inquiétant*, *important*, *nécessaire*.

**A reason.** *parce que*, *car*, *puisque*. **Car** is a good one to have: it means the same as *parce que* and shows range.

Put together: *À mon avis, le sommeil est essentiel, car sans sommeil je ne peux pas me concentrer.*

To say you disagree: *je ne suis pas d'accord*, *par contre* (on the other hand), *cependant* (however).

visuals.alt: A table of opinion phrases, precise adjectives and connectives to use instead of c'est bien

steps.text: *Le sport, c'est bien.* — low: vague adjective, no reason
*Je pense que le sport est bien parce que c'est important.* — better, but *bien* and *important* say nothing
*À mon avis, le sport est essentiel pour la santé mentale, car ça réduit le stress.*
steps.note: Precise adjective, a purpose with **pour**, a reason with **car**

check.prompt: Which is the strongest opinion sentence?
check.solution: Length is the same across all four; only the first has content. It varies the opinion phrase (**selon moi**), uses a precise adjective (**essentiel**), gives a reason with **car**, and uses a reflexive verb. The others pad with **bien**, which is the habit this step exists to break.
options: Selon moi, le sommeil est essentiel, car sans sommeil je me sens mal
Je pense que le sommeil est bien, parce que le sommeil est très bien
J'aime bien le sommeil et le sommeil est bien pour moi et pour les autres
Le sommeil, c'est bien, et c'est bien de dormir, parce que c'est bien

steps.title: Your turn: the vocabulary you need cold
steps.body:
Everything in this topic rests on knowing these without stopping to think. Reveal each one only after you have tried to say it, and use the speaker to check how it sounds.

A warning about one of them: **écouter** needs no preposition. *J'écoute de la musique*, never *j'écoute à la musique*. English hides the trap, because we say *listen **to***.

visuals.fallback: Cover the English and test yourself on: la santé mentale, le bien-être, le sommeil, le stress, inquiet, fatigué, détendu, heureux, triste, le soutien, se détendre, se coucher, se reposer, se sentir, dormir.

check.prompt: Translate into French: *I rest.* Use *se reposer*.
check.solution: **Je me repose.** Reflexive pronoun **me**, then the *-er* ending for *je*, which is **-e**.

steps.title: Grade 9: more than one tense, and the traps
steps.body:
At grade 9 the examiner is looking for **range**, and the fastest way to show it is more than one tense in the same answer. Even at this stage of Year 10 you have three:

- **Present**: *normalement, je me couche tôt*
- **Perfect** (from Year 9): *hier, je me suis couché tard*
- **Near future**: *demain, je vais me coucher tôt*

One sentence with all three, signalled by *normalement*, *hier* and *demain*, is worth more than a paragraph in the present.

Four traps in this topic, and they cost marks every year:

1. **écouter** takes no preposition: *j'écoute de la musique*.
2. **beaucoup de**, **plus de**, **trop de** always take **de**, never *des*: *beaucoup de devoirs*.
3. **Pour** + infinitive keeps your own reflexive pronoun: *pour **me** détendre*.
4. **ne … pas** wraps around the pronoun **and** the verb: *je **ne** me sens **pas** bien*.

And the free mark: make the adjective agree with you. *Fatiguée* if you are female, every time.

steps.text: *Normalement, je me couche à dix heures.* — present
*Mais hier, je me suis couché à minuit parce que j'avais beaucoup de devoirs.* — perfect, plus an imperfect
*Demain, je vais me reposer.* — near future
Three tenses, three time markers, one short paragraph
steps.note: This is what a grade 9 answer looks like at this point in Year 10

rows: je me ne sens pas bien
je ne me sens pas bien
props.title: Four traps

visuals.alt: A table of four common mistakes in this topic with the correct version of each

check.solution: **Beaucoup de** never takes *des*, and **ne** goes before the reflexive pronoun: *je ne me sens pas bien*.
options: J'ai beaucoup de devoirs, donc je ne me sens pas bien
J'ai beaucoup des devoirs, donc je ne me sens pas bien
J'ai beaucoup de devoirs, donc je me ne sens pas bien
J'ai beaucoup des devoirs, donc je me sens ne pas bien

steps.title: Summary
steps.body:
- **Feeling**: *je suis* + adjective for a state, *je me sens* + adjective for right now. The adjective **agrees** with you.
- **Reflexive verbs** carry a pronoun before the verb: je **me**, tu **te**, il/elle/on **se**, nous **nous**, vous **vous**, ils/elles **se**. It shortens before a vowel: *je m'habille*.
- **Se sentir** takes the short *-ir* pattern: *je me sens*, *nous nous sentons*.
- **Negative**: **ne** before the pronoun, **pas** after the verb — *je ne me sens pas bien*.
- **Pour** + infinitive is *in order to*, and keeps your own pronoun: *pour me détendre*.
- **Il faut** + infinitive is *you must*; **il ne faut pas** is *you must not*. It never changes form.
- **J'ai besoin de** + infinitive is *I need to*. Keep the **de**.
- **Opinions**: vary the phrase (*à mon avis*, *selon moi*, *je trouve que*), use a precise adjective, and always give a reason with *parce que* or *car*.
- **Range wins marks**: put present, perfect and near future in the same answer, signalled with *normalement*, *hier* and *demain*.
- **Traps**: *écouter* takes no preposition; *beaucoup de* not *des*; the pronoun in *pour me détendre*; and adjective agreement.

rows: je ne me sens pas bien
props.title: Everything in one place

visuals.alt: A summary table of the key structures in this topic with an example of each

questions.prompt: Translate into English: **je me sens fatigué**.
questions.solution: **Je me sens fatigué** — *I feel tired*. **Se sentir** is reflexive, so the **me** is part of the verb and is not translated separately.

questions.prompt: Which is the correct reflexive pronoun: *je ___ sens bien*?
questions.solution: With **je** the reflexive pronoun is **me**: *je me sens bien*. Te goes with tu, se with il/elle/on and ils/elles, nous with nous.
options: me
te
se
nous

questions.solution: **Je suis stressé** — *I am stressed*. Note it is **être**, not *avoir*, for this one.
**Le sommeil** is *sleep*. The verb is **dormir**, to sleep. Do not confuse it with *l'été*, summer.
options: sleep
sadness
support
summer

questions.prompt: Translate into French: **I relax**. Use the verb *se détendre*.
questions.solution: **Je me détends.** Two things to get right: the reflexive pronoun **me**, and the *-re* verb ending, which for **je** is **-s** on the stem *détend-*.

questions.prompt: Complete in French: *Je me couche __ dix heures* (at ten o'clock). Give the missing word.
questions.solution: **à** — *je me couche à dix heures*. Times take **à**: à sept heures, à midi, à minuit.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly gives a reason?
questions.solution: **Parce que** is two words and always keeps the **que**. *Pourquoi* asks *why*; it does not answer it.
options: Je fais du sport parce que ça me détend
Je fais du sport parce ça me détend
Je fais du sport que ça me détend
Je fais du sport pourquoi ça me détend

questions.prompt: Translate into English: **il faut dormir huit heures par nuit**.
questions.solution: **Il faut** + infinitive means *you must* or *it is necessary to*. It never changes its form, and **par nuit** is *a night*, not *by night*.

markScheme.description: you must / it is necessary to sleep

accepted: you must sleep eight hours a night
it is necessary to sleep eight hours a night
one must sleep eight hours a night
you need to sleep eight hours a night
you have to sleep eight hours a night

questions.prompt: Which is the correct present tense of **se sentir** for *nous*?
questions.solution: Both words are **nous**: the subject and the reflexive pronoun. Then the *-ir* ending for nous is **-ons** on the stem *sent-*.
options: nous nous sentons
nous se sentons
nous nous sentez
nous nous sens

questions.solution: **Je suis inquiet** (or **inquiète** if you are female). Adjectives agree with the person speaking, which is a mark in the writing paper.

questions.prompt: Translate into French: **I go to bed early because I need to sleep.**
questions.solution: **Je me couche tôt parce que j'ai besoin de dormir.** Three things carry the marks: the reflexive **me couche**, the connective **parce que**, and **avoir besoin de** + infinitive, which is *to need to*. *J'ai besoin dormir* without the **de** loses a mark.
accepted: je me couche tôt parce que j'ai besoin de dormir
je me couche tot parce que j'ai besoin de dormir
je me couche tôt car j'ai besoin de dormir
je me couche tot car j'ai besoin de dormir
je me couche tôt parce que je dois dormir
je me couche tot parce que je dois dormir

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses two tenses correctly?
questions.solution: **Normalement** signals the present; **hier** signals the perfect. Reflexive verbs take **être** in the perfect, so it is *je me suis couché*, and the past participle agrees with the subject.
options: Normalement je me couche tôt, mais hier je me suis couché tard
Normalement je me couche tôt, mais hier je me couche tard
Normalement je me suis couché tôt, mais hier je me couche tard
Normalement je me couchais tôt, mais hier je me couche tard

questions.prompt: Translate into French: **I would like to do more sport.**
questions.solution: **Je voudrais faire plus de sport.** **Je voudrais** is the polite conditional of *vouloir* and is followed straight by the infinitive. **Plus de** takes **de**, never *du*, before a noun.
accepted: je voudrais faire plus de sport

questions.prompt: Which gives the most developed opinion?
questions.solution: All four are about the same length, so length is no guide. The first is the only one that says anything: an opinion phrase (**je trouve que**), a precise adjective (**essentiel**), a purpose (**pour la santé mentale**) and a reason (**car ça réduit le stress**). The other three repeat **bien**, which carries no meaning, and repeating a vague word at length scores no better than saying it once.
options: Je trouve que le sport est essentiel pour la santé mentale, car ça réduit le stress
Je pense que le sport est bien et je pense aussi que le sport est très bien
J'aime beaucoup le sport parce que c'est bien et c'est bien pour tout le monde
Le sport est bien, et c'est bien de faire du sport, parce que c'est très bien

questions.prompt: Give the French for **in my opinion** — the phrase beginning with *à*.
questions.solution: **À mon avis.** Learn a range so you are not repeating *je pense que*: **selon moi**, **je trouve que**, **d'après moi**.

questions.prompt: Écrivez environ 50 mots en français sur votre santé mentale. Mentionnez ce que vous faites pour vous détendre et pourquoi.
questions.solution: Level-marked on content and language. A strong answer covers both parts of the question, uses at least one reflexive verb, gives a reason with **parce que** or **car**, and includes an opinion phrase. Aim for two or three sentences on each bullet rather than a list of single clauses.

markScheme.description: Content: both parts of the question covered, with some development
Language: range of vocabulary and structures, accurate verb forms and agreements

criteria.text: Both parts answered: what you do to relax, and why
At least one reflexive verb used correctly, for example je me détends or je me couche
A reason given with parce que or car, and an opinion phrase such as à mon avis
Accurate verb endings and adjective agreement, with a range of vocabulary rather than one repeated structure

questions.modelAnswer: À mon avis, la santé mentale est très importante. Normalement, je me couche à dix heures parce que j'ai besoin de dormir. Pour me détendre, j'écoute de la musique et je fais du sport avec mes amis, car ça réduit le stress. Quand je suis stressé, je parle à ma famille. Je trouve que c'est essentiel.

questions.prompt: Translate into French: **you must not work all the time** (use *il ne faut pas*).
questions.solution: **Il ne faut pas travailler tout le temps.** The negative wraps around **faut**: *ne … pas*. The infinitive **travailler** then follows unchanged.
accepted: il ne faut pas travailler tout le temps

questions.prompt: Traduisez en français: *I am often stressed because I have a lot of homework. To relax, I listen to music and I go to bed early.*
questions.solution: **Je suis souvent stressé parce que j'ai beaucoup de devoirs. Pour me détendre, j'écoute de la musique et je me couche tôt.** The traps: **beaucoup de** takes *de* not *des*; **pour** + infinitive keeps the reflexive pronoun (**pour me détendre**); and *écouter* needs no preposition, so it is *j'écoute de la musique*, never *j'écoute à*.

markScheme.description: parce que j'ai beaucoup de devoirs

criteria.text: parce que j'ai beaucoup de devoirs, with **de** not *des*
Pour me détendre, keeping the reflexive pronoun
j'écoute de la musique et je me couche tôt

questions.modelAnswer: Je suis souvent stressé parce que j'ai beaucoup de devoirs. Pour me détendre, j'écoute de la musique et je me couche tôt.

examTechnique.body:
This is the first topic of Year 10, and it sets the habits for the rest of the course. Vocabulary has to be known cold, because a word you have to stop and think about costs time in every skill. Grammar marks come from three things this term: reflexive pronouns, adjective agreement, and getting the negative in the right place.

In writing and speaking, the marks split between **content** and **language**. Content means answering every part of the question, with development rather than a list. Language means range: more than one tense, varied opinion phrases, connectives beyond *et* and *mais*. A short answer that does both beats a long one that stays in the present.

**Accents matter.** Write *é* where it belongs. The app accepts an answer typed without accents so a keyboard does not block you, but the solution always shows the accented spelling, and the exam expects it.
examinerErrors: Dropping the reflexive pronoun: *je couche* instead of *je me couche*. The pronoun is part of the verb.
Putting the negative in the wrong place: *je me ne sens pas bien*. The **ne** goes before the pronoun — *je ne me sens pas bien*.
Writing *j'écoute à la musique*. **Écouter** takes no preposition, however strongly the English *listen to* suggests one.
Using *des* after a quantity: *beaucoup des devoirs*. **Beaucoup de**, **plus de** and **trop de** always take **de**.
Forgetting adjective agreement. A girl writes *fatiguée*, and it is a written mark that sounds identical.
Losing the pronoun after **pour**: *pour se détendre* when talking about yourself. It should be *pour me détendre*.
Filling an answer with *c'est bien*. A precise adjective and a reason are worth far more than another vague opinion.
examTechnique.grade9Looks: A grade 9 answer at this point in Year 10 puts more than one tense into a short paragraph, signalled clearly with *normalement*, *hier* and *demain*, and never leaves an opinion without a reason. Its opinion phrases vary rather than repeating *je pense que*, and its adjectives are precise: *essentiel*, *inquiétant*, *nécessaire* rather than *bien*. Reflexive pronouns and adjective agreements are right without apparent effort, and the negative wraps the pronoun and the verb correctly. It answers every part of the question with development, not a list.
